requirements.requirement: Repair telemetry-heartbeat.service so it runs the installed /usr/local/bin/telemetry-heartbeat program as svc-heartbeat.
requirements.summary: The effective ExecStart was corrected from the missing path to the installed program. The service was directly observed active and running that program under svc-heartbeat both before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Refresh /run/telemetry-heartbeat/heartbeat at least every five seconds.
requirements.summary: A bounded six-second observation showed the heartbeat advancing with a final age of one second. After reboot it advanced again over two seconds and had an age of zero seconds.
The program's SHA-256 hash matched the preparation baseline before the repair, after service startup, and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the existing svc-heartbeat service identity and service security restrictions.
requirements.summary: User and group remained svc-heartbeat. The original hardening directives—including NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, strict filesystem protection, empty capability bounding set, restricted address families, and the narrow writable path—remained effective before and after reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: node1 had a healthy pre-restart state, the reboot was acknowledged, its boot ID changed from f38484ef-a289-4d30-9a94-4ab42c44f900 to 2915c282-8fbc-43a0-a7ca-accaa2ae9d04, and the enabled service, identity, program, and refreshing heartbeat recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the reboot.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. cmd-8c848027bdd54232 made the narrowly scoped required unit-file correction, reloaded systemd, and restarted the repaired service. cmd-85cc064c647e4cd8 created a transient reboot job and rebooted node1 solely for the mandatory restart protocol; its transient units did not persist across reboot. The final lifecycle snapshot shows no failed services, unchanged network exposure and healthy package state. New systemd-private temporary directories are expected consequences of reboot and the preserved PrivateTmp restriction, not abandoned residue.
